jobs.title: Senior Technical Recruiter
jobs.description_text: The Role Recruiting for Normal is a specialist's craft several times over. AI/ML researchers, DV and silicon engineers, and systems software engineers are each small candidate pools where every strong person is fielding multiple offers — and the people you're hunting can smell a recruiter who doesn't speak their language. As a Sr. Technical Recruiter, you will work on full-cycle recruiting across Normal's roles: AI/ML research and engineering, silicon (architects, RTL and DV engineers, physical design, bring-up), systems software, and the G&A roles that keep a scaling company running. You will partner directly with hiring managers who are themselves deep in their craft, source candidates who aren't looking, and close people who have every option. This is a seat on a growing talent team where your searches directly determine whether a chip tapes out on schedule. What You'll Own - Full-Cycle Recruiting: Manage the end-to-end recruitment process across AI/ML, silicon and ASIC, and software roles from intake through close, flexing to G&A searches as priorities shift. - Strategic Sourcing: Identify and engage top-tier talent across AI research, unconventional silicon architecture, design verification, and systems software: people who are rarely on the market and need a reason to talk. - Hiring Manager Partnership: Act as a strategic partner to hiring managers across engineering, research, and business functions, aligning on candidate qualifications, technical bars, and calibration

jobs.title: Recruiting Coordinator
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE You will own the operational backbone of how Normal hires. As our Recruiting Coordinator, you keep every candidate moving, every interview scheduled, and every system the talent team runs on humming, from first touch to signed offer, where People Operations takes the baton. You sit at the center of the recruiting process, working directly with recruiters, hiring managers, and candidates across five offices and multiple time zones, and you work as the right hand to our Head of Talent: when he's buried, you're the person he leans on. This is a hands-on coordination role with room to grow into recruiting operations. You will run interview scheduling and coordination, keep Ashby clean and reliable as our system of record, and make sure offers, reports, and candidate communications move without friction. As the team and its systems mature, your ownership of systems and process grows with them. The work is high-volume, detail-dense, and global. Great looks like a candidate who never feels the seams, a hiring manager who always has what they need, and a recruiting operation that runs on rails. WHAT YOU'LL OWN - Interview Scheduling & Coordination: Schedule and reschedule single and multi-panel interviews across candidates, interviewers, and time zones. jobs.title: Hardware Engineer, Physical Design
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE As a Physical Design Engineer at Normal, you will own the end-to-end silicon realization path, taking complex architectures from synthesis and physical floorplanning all the way through timing signoff and GDSII tapeout. Sitting at the intersection of custom ASIC design and our hardware-algorithm co-designed systems, you will shape physical feasibility early in the design cycle by working shoulder-to-shoulder with RTL and architecture teams. You'll drive the full backend implementation flow—optimizing floorplanning, place-and-route (P&R), clock tree synthesis (CTS), static timing analysis (STA), and physical verification (DRC/LVS) to achieve aggressive power, performance, and area (PPA) targets. We are looking for a seasoned engineer who thrives in cross-functional environments and takes pride in tapeout-proven execution. The ideal candidate brings a meticulous approach to physical signoff, maintains clarity in fast-paced build cycles, and is excited to solve the physical constraints of novel computing architectures. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Physical Implementation & Flow: Lead the full netlist-to-GDSII physical design flow, including floorplanning, power grid design, placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), and place-and-route (P&R). - Timing Closure & STA: Own static timing analysis (STA), timing constraints creation/validation, and signoff timing closure across all operating corners and modes. - Power, Area, and Signal Integrity: Drive physical optimization for power, per

jobs.title: Systems/Rack Architect
jobs.description_text: The Role As the Systems/Rack Architect, you will lead the system architecture design of Normal’s AI compute hardware end-to-end, from initial concept to specification, design reviews, integration, and deployment. You will guide system-level decisions spanning boards, chassis, interconnects, and rack-scale system design, collaborating closely across hardware, software, and other engineering teams to ensure system designs meet performance and workload requirements. You’ll define system requirements and specifications, evaluate architectural options, and drive key technical decisions as our hardware platforms evolve. You’ll evaluate partner and vendor designs against our requirements, identify technical gaps and schedule risks early, and lead system-level tradeoffs. You’ll play a central role in bringing these pieces together into cohesive, high-performance AI compute systems and driving the overall system from architecture through deployment. What You Will Own - Lead hardware system architecture from initial concept and requirements through design reviews, integration, and production deployment. - Translate workload and performance requirements into hardware decisions, working closely with cross-functional teams and external partners. - Lead architecture design across boards, chassis, and racks, including system topology, power, thermal, scale-up and scale-out fabrics, and networking. - Define and own bring-up, system integration, validation and qualification strategy. jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE We’re hiring a Platform Engineer to own and evolve the critical infrastructure that powers Normal’s engineering organization. While our infrastructure is distributed across multiple locations, this position involves managing the local physical infrastructure (network, servers) and requires regular on-site presence in Mountain View and occasional travels to the New York office. This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role for someone with deep systems knowledge and broad infrastructure experience. You’ll work across Linux systems, networking, storage, security, automation, deployment infrastructure, and open-source tooling, taking ownership of complex systems and solving problems that don’t always fit neatly into one technical domain. We’re looking for someone who understands infrastructure from the ground up, has strong technical judgment, and is comfortable operating independently in a fast-moving startup environment. Leadership is not required, impact through technical depth, ownership, and execution is. jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE As an early-career Product Manager, you'll work with the Product Lead and the engineering teams to help build the AI systems and autoresearch platform our ASIC team needs to tapeout unconventional, physics-based architecture. We are rethinking the chip design system from the ground up, automating the process of research: exploring the full design space, generating candidate architectures, evaluating them at appropriate levels of fidelity, and feeding learnings from experiments run in hardware labs and deployed silicon into the next generation chip. Domains of exploration include RTL optimization, design verification, and continual learning from experiment results. You'll help decide what we build, then be accountable for delivering on the incremental milestones to tapeout. On any given day, you might sit with a chip architect benchmarking novel architectures, shadow a verification debug session and come back with a proposal for what to automate, scope out the requirements and success criteria for a custom EDA tool, or prototype an experiment dashboard. This is a building role. You'll write specs, run experiments, and use coding agents to prototype and land fixes yourself. When you have an idea, we would rather you spend an afternoon prototyping a rough version than a week describing it. No semiconductor background is required to start. You will own the schedule across the entire product development lifecycle: silicon, systems and software. jobs.title: Runtime Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. The runtime is the layer the rest of that software runs through: it is how compiled programs get loaded, scheduled, and executed on our hardware. You will own its design and much of its implementation, and set its technical direction. This is a senior, hands-on role. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will build the runtime against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, behind one interface, so that software above the runtime doesn't change when silicon arrives. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Runtime Architecture: Own the design of the runtime: device management, memory allocation and host-device transfer, executable loading, and command submission. Success means the compiler and serving layers program our hardware through one stable interface. - Hardware Abstraction: Hide the differences between simulators, FPGA prototypes, silicon, and later hardware generations behind that interface. - Device State: Manage the state that lives on our hardware between requests, such as resident model weights, so the serving layer can rely on it. - Performance: Keep runtime overhead off the critical path for LLM inference, measured by end-to-end latency and throughput. - Cross-Team Interfaces: Define the boundary with the compiler above the runtime, and with the driver an

This is a critical role at the intersection of semiconductor manufacturing, commercial strategy and supply chain execution. You will own our foundry commercial relationships, negotiate manufacturing capacity agreements, secure production capacity and drive competitive silicon economics as we transition from prototype silicon to scaled manufacturing. You will work closely with Silicon Engineering, Systems Engineering, Product, Finance and Manufacturing Operations, translating technical requirements and production forecasts into commercially robust supplier commitments. This is an opportunity to build the foundry sourcing capability of a high-growth semiconductor company from the ground up. The role sits in Manufacturing & Operations and reports to the Head of Manufacturing & Operations. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Foundry strategy and supplier relationships: Develop foundry sourcing strategies aligned with Normal's silicon roadmap, manufacturing requirements and long-term production plans; lead commercial supplier engagement, negotiations, business reviews and escalations; evaluate sourcing alternatives and develop contingency strategies to manage concentration, geographic, capacity and technology risks. - Commercial negotiations and contracting: Establish and negotiate clear contractua

jobs.title: Compiler Backend Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Getting a model correct on that hardware is the frontend's job; making it fast is yours. Our hardware does not look like a CPU or GPU, so its compiler backend can't be borrowed from one. As a Compiler Engineer focused on the backend, you will help design and build the custom compilation that maps LLM inference onto it, from scheduling and memory planning to the code our hardware actually executes. You will work at the boundary between the compiler and the hardware, closely enough to know when an optimization belongs at a different layer, or when the right answer is a new abstraction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will measure your work against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Code Generation: Build the passes that turn lowered programs into the code our hardware executes, designing new compilation approaches where conventional ones don't fit. Success means correct, efficient code for every operation our models need. - Scheduling and Memory Planning: Own how work and data are scheduled and placed across our hardware's resources, measured by utilization and end-to-end latency on LLM inference. - Fusion and Dispatch: Own fusion and dispatch decisions for LLM inference, so the hardwar

jobs.title: Technical Content Lead
jobs.description_text: YOUR ROLE IN OUR MISSION We are hiring a Technical Content Lead: a deep-tech journalist or an in-house writer with equivalent technical depth, editorial judgment and a strong publishing record, to explain the science and engineering behind Normal Inference Systems. You will help establish language for an unfamiliar architecture and make its performance and applications understandable to technical and commercial audiences. You will work directly with scientists, researchers and engineers, read the underlying papers and results, and learn challenging new science every day. You will hold the pen on blog posts, social copy, research stories, technical essays and evaluation materials, while helping engineers and researchers craft and improve their own content. Alongside the hardware, you will own research communications for Normal's frontier applied AI research program, which develops AI methods for silicon design and verification. This is a senior individual-contributor role reporting to the Head of Communications and embedded with Engineering. You will be the Communications and Marketing team's subject-matter expert on technical content, progress and the hardware roadmap. Original technical writing and editorial partnership with technical experts are the core of the role, with other projects prioritized with the Head of Communications. jobs.title: Memory Architect
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal is building AI inference hardware based on our revolutionary new Thermo In-Memory Computing architecture and as Memory Architect you will lead the translation of these concepts from theory into silicon. You will have free rein to completely reimagine each element of a conventional memory; from the design and layout read/write paths, organization of memory arrays, to the development of a microarchitecture which seamlessly interleaves core memory operations with high performance compute. Ultimately, you will be responsible for delivering 100-1000× improvements in performance in AI inference. You will report to the Director of Silicon Engineering and partner with scientists, microarchitects, physical design, and analog design engineers to implement a new standard cell library which combines existing digital compute primitives with Normal’s ThermoDRAM compute primitives. You will translate these new compute primitives into a highly performant Compute In-Memory System. You will own the technical relationship with major manufacturers from PDK acquisition through tapeout of test chips and production silicon. This role requires a seasoned engineer with prior experience in memory technology but who understands that radical performance improvements require radical paradigm shifts. jobs.title: Hardware Engineer, Performance Modeling
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE As a Performance Modeling Engineer at Normal, you will build the transaction-level model (TLM) of our physics-inspired ASICs. It is the model that sits between RTL and the rest of our modeling stack, and that both our architects and our verification team rely on. You will own the path from RTL to the numerical performance results. You will correlate the TLM against RTL, FPGA prototypes, and synthesis results, then turn it into calibrated latency, bandwidth and energy parameters for kernel-level models. You will work closely with the architecture, hardware design and DV teams, using their feedback to help refine our end-to-end system. The through-line is your modeling expertise, applied to an architecture that computes differently from anything you have modeled before, and to the AI that is changing how AI workloads get done. This is a seat for a performance modeling engineer who wants their craft to compound rather than repeat. Ultimately Normal Computing will build a next generation system with 100-1000× improvement in AI inference, and your work will make this possible. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Transaction-Level Model: Build and maintain a cycle-accurate approximate TLM of our compute tiles, memory hierarchy, and interconnect in an appropriate language (SystemC, C++ or Python). The code must be fast enough to simulate real workloads and accurate enough to make production design decisions - Feeding the Modeling Stack: Translate TLM and RTL results combined with physical

jobs.title: Head of Silicon Product Engineering
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal builds custom silicon for AI inference. As Head of Silicon Product Engineering, you will own everything that happens between a design being correct and a product being real: packaging, test and ATE, post-silicon validation and bring-up, yield and qualification, OSAT and test-house selection, and production calibration and screening of our memory products. This is a build role. You will stand up the team, the vendor relationships, and the processes that take Normal’s silicon from tape-out through high-volume manufacturing, working at the intersection of design, manufacturing, and product to turn architectural intent into a producible, testable, reliable product at scale. You will also be setting precedent: establishing test and calibration methodology for a new silicon program as it matures toward volume. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Post-Silicon Strategy: Own end-to-end bring-up, characterization, validation, and debug across multiple silicon generations. - Packaging & Test: Define and drive packaging and test strategy, including ATE program development, test coverage, and test condition optimization for yield, quality, and performance. - OSAT & Test-House Selection: Select, qualify, and manage OSAT and test-house partners; own the relationship through NPI and into high-volume manufacturing, including cost, quality, and yield negotiations. - Yield & Qualification: Lead yield learning and qualification efforts from early silicon through production ramp, including root-c

jobs.title: Hardware Engineer, DFT
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE As a Design-for-Test (DFT) Engineer at Normal, you will own the DFT architecture and implementation for our next-generation, physics-inspired ASICs, from early RTL design through tapeout and silicon bring-up. You will define and drive scan/ATPG, memory built-in self-test (MBIST), and boundary-scan strategies, working closely with RTL, verification, physical design, and silicon product engineering teams. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with end-to-end ownership of silicon testability. You will establish DFT methodologies, guide external implementation partners, and ensure our designs are ready for manufacturing test. You’ll work on unconventional computing architectures where testability must be considered from the beginning, with the opportunity to shape the DFT infrastructure for an entirely new class of silicon. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - DFT Architecture: Define and own chip-level DFT architecture, including scan insertion, ATPG, scan compression, MBIST, boundary scan/JTAG, and test access infrastructure. - Implementation & Integration: Drive DFT insertion and integration across RTL, synthesis, and physical design, ensuring testability requirements are met without compromising power, performance, or area. - Test Coverage & Signoff: Own DFT verification, ATPG pattern generation, fault coverage analysis, test-mode validation, and DFT signoff through tapeout. - Manufacturing Test Readiness: Partner with the Head of Silicon Product Engineering to deliver product

jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE As a Firmware Engineer at Normal, you will create low-level software to run on our SOC to provide an interface between our physics-inspired ASICs and higher software levels. You will have to develop code that runs on a microcontroller that provides an API layer for upper software levels to exercise our AI acceleration hardware. You will interface with the hardware and software design teams, understanding both the hardware and software architectures. You will debug in various prototyping and ASIC environments. For this role, you also have to specify and create the development environment. The through-line is your firmware expertise, applied to silicon and software stacks that compute differently from anything you have coded for before. This is a seat for a firmware engineer who wants their craft to compound rather than repeat. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Development of firmware for an embedded processor on an SOC: Create firmware to support an API that bridges higher-level software to the hardware layer. - Work with software and hardware: Collaborate with software and hardware engineers to understand and specify the API requirements. - Creation of the development environment: Acquire and configure appropriate tools to create the firmware, including compilers, simulators, and debuggers. Work across multiple development environments including software simulation, RTL simulation, and physical hardware. - Verification of the firmware to a production level: Develop a verification

jobs.title: Simulator & Debug Tools Lead
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Nothing off the shelf simulates it, so the tool our compiler and hardware teams depend on to validate their work before silicon exists has to be built, not bought. As our Simulator & Debug Tools Lead, you will own that simulator, along with the debugging and profiling tools that integrate with our compiler. Fidelity, speed, and tooling all compete for the same hours, and you will decide where those hours go, keeping the rest of the team honest about what the chip can actually do. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Simulator Architecture: Own the architecture and roadmap of our hardware simulator, including accuracy, performance, and coverage of new hardware features as they land. Success means compiler and runtime work never waits on hardware. - Behavioral Correctness: Make the simulator's behavior, state, and memory semantics trustworthy enough that compiler and runtime engineers can act on what it tells them. - Debug and Profiling Tools: Build the debuggers, tracers, and profilers engineers actually reach for, measured by how quickly the team can find and fix a bug. - Hardware Correlation: Partner with our Design Verification and bring-up teams to correlate the simulator with RTL, FPGA prototypes, and eventually silicon, and close the loop when they disagree

jobs.title: Compiler Frontend Engineer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Our compiler is how models reach that hardware, and new LLM architectures show up faster than most compilers can track. A new attention variant, MoE routing scheme, or quantization approach has to be represented faithfully in our compiler before it can run, let alone run fast. As a Compiler Engineer focused on frontend and model bring-up, you will extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes so new LLM architectures are supported before a customer asks for them. This is a research-adjacent seat: you are expected to follow the literature closely, and publish on behalf of Normal. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will validate bring-up against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, so that models are ready to run when silicon arrives. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Model Bring-up: Bring up frontend and mid-level support for new LLM architectures in our compiler, from attention variants to MoE routing schemes. Success means new architectures run correctly on our stack soon after release, ahead of customer demand. - IR and Lowering: Extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes to represent new architectural primitives faithfully rather than approximately, with test coverage that keeps them correct as the compiler evolves. - Quantization and Numerics: Represent the quan

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer, Hardware Systems
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal is building AI inference hardware based on our Thermo In-Memory Computing architecture, designed to deliver orders-of-magnitude more efficient compute. As the founding mechanical engineer on our hardware team, you will define the physical design of that hardware at every level of integration, from the accelerator through the server to the rack. You will help determine what fits, what can be cooled, what can be serviced, and where an existing supplier platform does the job. You report to the head of our hardware systems organization and partner with our silicon, systems, and deployment engineers, and with the external design and manufacturing partners who build to our drawings. We're looking for someone who thrives on turning a system architecture into hardware and takes pride in catching the problem before the build does. The form factor, thermal envelope, mounting, and serviceability decisions you make set the foundation for the systems Normal ships, and the hardware you define is the hardware our customers run. Candidates from OEM and ODM server teams, hyperscaler infrastructure teams, and earlier-stage hardware companies could all be well qualified for this role. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Mechanical Design: Own the electromechanical design of our inference hardware as it moves from engineering configuration to deployable product, including form factor, thermal solution and airflow, connectors and cabling, and the power and thermal envelope it has to live within.

You will work with senior leaders, VIP guests and production partners to bring Normal’s work to the world stage. You care about the craft of engaging in-person experiences. jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.description_text: THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication. Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes. THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip. You'll work on this as a co-design problem. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, so your findings feed architectural decisions r

jobs.title: 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist to join our Research Team in London. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system. An inference worker can return tokens from a cheaper model, or a highly quantized version of the one it's supposed to run. Even with the right model, it can sample with the wrong parameters. Training faces its own attacks, and Agora showed what a permissionless run deals with in practice: participants who disrupt training by dropping updates or flooding the system, free-riders who submit trivial work and collect the rewards, poisoned updates that plant backdoors, attempts to extract private data from gradients and activations, and contributors who inflate their reported work to claim rewards they didn't earn. jobs.description_text: Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. This setting breaks nearly every assumption of datacenter training: communication-efficient training across different parallelism axes, fault tolerance as nodes join and drop mid-run, heterogeneous compute and networks, and robustness to malicious participants. Our published methods include Subspace Networks https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01260, Factored Gossip DiLoCo https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22768, AsyncMesh https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22442, and Sentinel https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03592. As a Research Scientist you'll build the training system that takes Protocol Learning from the 8B run to frontier scale: large models on heterogeneous hardware, in physically different regions, connected by ordinary internet. jobs.description_text: OUR MISSION SPAN develops products that accelerate the rapid adoption of renewable energy in the home. The flagship SPAN Smart Panel is the first true evolution for the traditional home electric panel, harnessing enhanced technology for metering, monitoring, and control. An expanded product suite of intelligent, integrated solutions radically lowers the cost and complexity of energy upgrades–including solar, batteries and EVs–empowering homeowners to be active, resilient and informed players in the energy market. THE TEAM AND ROLE SPAN's Device Software team is responsible for all of the software that is physically embodied in our hardware products. The Gen3 SPAN Panel is a distributed system of STM32H5 (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontroller modules that talk over CAN, meter power in real time, and open or close relays that sit directly between the grid, the home and its solar, battery and EV equipment. When that firmware makes a decision, real current moves. We are building a dedicated Functional Safety (FuSa) firmware capability to take Gen3 firmware through certification as a Power Control System under UL 3141 and as Class B control software under UL/IEC 60730-1 Annex H. This is not a checkbox exercise: FuSa at SPAN spans how we architect and partition the firmware, how we detect faults and drive the system into defined safe states, how we test and prove coverage, and how we document and trace every safety requirement back to code. We are in detailed design with tooling in work, and we are looking for a structures design engineer to own parts on that aircraft from concept through first article. You will design and size real hardware: control surfaces, ribs and spars, frames, doors and access panels, fittings and joints. You will take your parts all the way out, through analysis, drawings, vendor coordination, first article, and the fixes that come after. Our structures lead sets the architecture and the design approach. Inside that, your parts are yours. This is a role for someone who wants to design more and coordinate less. You will be in CAD and in FEA most days, and in the shop the rest of them. The aircraft is small enough as an organization that the person who draws a part is the person who sees it come off the tool, and finds out the same week whether the call they made was right. jobs.title: AWS Security Architect, GovCloud / IL5
jobs.description_text: Role Overview Swarm Aero is hiring an Information Security Lead / AWS Security Architect to sit within the IT organization and own the security architecture, documentation, and compliance support needed across our AWS environment and regulated customer deployments. This is a dedicated IT role. The person will work closely with Legion because Legion has the most urgent IL5/IL6 deployment needs, but they are not a Legion-owned resource. They will support the existing company-wide SSP and CMMC program while also helping build and maintain the separate Legion-specific security package required for high-side and government cloud deployments. The right person needs to be comfortable moving between implementation and documentation. This is not just a paperwork role. They need to understand how AWS is architected, how controls are actually implemented, how to produce evidence, how to drive remediation, and how to keep the broader security program aligned as Legion moves into IL5/IL6 environments. This is a remote role, with 1 week onsite in D.C. a month. jobs.title: Composites Technician
jobs.description_text: About the Role We're building real aircraft structure today, and we're scaling the shop that builds it. The processes exist. Making them better is the job. We're not looking for someone who just follows a layup schedule. We're looking for someone who reads one, sees the three things that could be done better, and proves it on the table. You'll work shoulder to shoulder with engineering on real aircraft hardware, and the best ideas about how we build tend to come off the floor first. jobs.title: Senior Systems Administrator
jobs.description_text: Role Overview: The Sr. Systems Administrator will be the primary point of contact for maintaining IT infrastructure, providing helpdesk support, and ensuring staff have the tools and technology they need to achieve maximum efficiency. This role requires a proactive, hands-on approach to day-to-day operations, focusing on end-user support, infrastructure management, and optimizing cloud and on-premises environments. This is a unique opportunity for an ambitious individual to grow with Swarm Aero. The role offers significant career advancement potential, exposure to cutting-edge cloud technologies, and the chance to take ownership of IT operations. You will have the opportunity to shape the IT environment and eventually become the primary IT leader for an expanding office of 50+ people. Mentorship, continuous learning, and skill development will be a core part of your experience here. This is a hybrid role, spending 3-days onsite in Oxnard at our headquarters. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Embedded
jobs.description_text: About the Role Most software engineers never see their code tested against reality. At Swarm Aero, that's the baseline. We are looking for a Forward Deployed Software Engineer to embed directly with U.S. government and military customers and own the technical success of our C2 systems in the field. You will be the person who makes our software work -- not in a lab, not in a staging environment, but in real operational contexts across domestic and international deployments. Austere locations, high-stakes timelines, and complex distributed systems are the job. This is a full-scope engineering role. You will build critical integrations, debug core services, contribute to new development, and ship solutions that warfighters and government operators depend on. If you want to write code that matters and see it run in environments most engineers never touch, this is the role. We need an engineer who can cross boundaries and work with all subsystems through avionics integration and validation. You will use this to generate highly effective communications in artifacts like white papers, proposals, presentations, and analysis for internal and external audiences. - Organize and scale: To organize is to create. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Real-Time Systems (Early Career)
jobs.description_text: Legion's Command & Control platform lets a single operator plan, direct, and execute missions across a networked swarm of heterogeneous aircraft, in real time, over intermittent comms, at a scale nobody else in the industry is attempting. That means distributed state under unreliable networks, dense telemetry moving fast enough to strain anything you've built before, and interfaces for a problem space that barely has prior art. You'll work across the stack, wherever the hard problem is that week. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build and ship features in the C2 system that directs swarms of heterogeneous aircraft - Work on systems that hold state and stay responsive when comms degrade or drop entirely - Move between the interface layer and the services behind it, following the problem rather than a job description - Prototype new ways to represent and control vehicle telemetry, sensor data, and scheduling - Take features end to end, from a rough problem statement through design, implementation, and deployment - Ship early and often, backed by strong CI/CD, QA, and DevSecOps WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent self-taught depth - Real strength in fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, concurrency, networking, systems - Evidence you've built something hard because you wanted to.
